cards.front: Recall a key point about Contract Law
cards.back: A contract is a legally binding agreement between two or more parties, enforceable in the courts

cards.front: Recall a key point about Contract Law
cards.back: Three elements are needed to form a contract: offer and acceptance, consideration, and intention to create legal relations

cards.front: Recall a key point about Contract Law
cards.back: An offer is a clear statement of terms on which the offeror is willing to be bound — it must be distinguished from an invitation to treat

cards.front: Recall a key point about Contract Law
cards.back: Acceptance must be an unqualified agreement to the exact terms of the offer — a counter-offer rejects the original offer

cards.front: Recall a key point about Contract Law
cards.back: Consideration is something of value exchanged between the parties — each party must give and receive something (but need not be equal)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Contract Law
cards.back: Intention to create legal relations means the parties must intend their agreement to be legally binding — social agreements are presumed not to bind

cards.front: Recall a key point about Contract Law
cards.back: Contract terms can be conditions (essential terms, breach allows termination), warranties (minor terms, breach allows damages only) or innominate terms

cards.front: Recall a key point about Contract Law
cards.back: Express terms are those specifically agreed by the parties; implied terms are read into the contract by law or custom

cards.front: Recall a key point about Contract Law
cards.back: Breach of contract occurs when one party fails to perform their obligations — the innocent party is entitled to remedies

cards.front: Recall a key point about Contract Law
cards.back: Damages are the main remedy — they aim to put the claimant in the position they would have been in had the contract been performed

cards.front: Recall a key point about Contract Law
cards.back: Specific performance is an order requiring the party in breach to perform their obligations — it is only available where damages are inadequate

cards.front: Recall a key point about Contract Law
cards.back: Injunction is a court order preventing a party from doing something that would breach the contract

cards.front: What should you know about gcse law exam tips — contract law?
cards.back: 1. For Contract Law questions, identify the relevant area of law and state the legal principles clearly 2. Apply legal rules to the facts of the scenario — don't just state the law 3. When evaluating, consider both the effectiveness and fairness of legal rules 4. Reference relevant cases and statutes when discussing Contract Law 5. Consider reform proposals and alternative approaches where relevant
